questions.def: Use 'lower' for comparative adjectives with one syllable.
questions.question: This year's profits are ___ than last year's.

questions.def: Use 'the most' for superlative adjectives with multiple syllables.
questions.question: She is ___ person I know.

questions.def: 'Good' is irregular; its superlative is 'best'.
questions.question: This is the ___ movie I have ever seen.

questions.def: Use 'the more... the better' for parallel increase.
questions.question: The ___ you practice, the better you get.

questions.def: 'The least' shows the lowest degree of expensiveness.
questions.question: This is ___ expensive restaurant in town.

questions.def: 'Bad' is irregular; its superlative is 'worst'.
questions.question: This is the ___ experience of my life.

questions.def: Use 'as + adjective + as' for equality.
questions.question: He is ___ as his sister.

questions.def: 'More and more' shows increasing difficulty.
questions.question: The situation is getting ___ difficult.

questions.def: 'Far' has two superlatives: 'farthest' and 'furthest'.
questions.question: This is the ___ I have ever traveled.

questions.def: 'Much' intensifies comparative adjectives.
questions.question: She is ___ younger than I expected.

questions.def: Use the comparative form for comparing two things.
questions.question: Which is ___, the Pacific or Atlantic?

questions.def: 'Nearest' is the superlative form of 'near'.
questions.question: This is the ___ station to my house.

questions.def: 'Least' is the superlative of 'little', meaning 'smallest amount'.
questions.question: The ___ expensive option is not always the best.

questions.def: Use 'as' in negative comparisons: 'not as/so...as'.
questions.question: She is not ___ intelligent as her brother.

questions.def: 'Oldest' is generally used for age, 'elder' for family relations.
questions.question: He is the ___ student in the class.

questions.def: Use 'more' for forming comparative adjectives.
questions.question: The project was ___ difficult than we thought.

questions.def: 'Far more' emphasizes the difference in reliability.
questions.question: This car is ___ reliable than my old one.

questions.def: 'Less' is the comparative form of 'little'.
questions.question: She has ___ experience than he does.

questions.def: Use 'the less... the happier' to show parallel decrease.
questions.question: The ___ I see him, the happier I am.

questions.def: Use 'the + comparative + of' when comparing two things.
questions.question: He is ___ the two brothers.

questions.def: 'Earliest' is the superlative form of 'early'.
questions.question: This is the ___ flight available.

questions.def: 'By far' is used to strongly emphasize a superlative.
questions.question: He is by ___ the best player on the team.

questions.def: 'Worse' is the comparative form of 'bad'.
questions.question: The result was ___ than expected.

questions.def: "Better attended" is the correct comparative form; avoid double comparatives.
questions.question: This year's conference was ___ than last year's.

questions.def: For superlative adjectives with 3+ syllables, use "the most + adjective".
questions.question: She is ___ person I've ever met.

questions.def: With 'of the two', use 'the + comparative'.
questions.question: Of the two options, this solution is the most practical choice.

questions.def: For most two-syllable adjectives, use "more" for the comparative.
questions.question: This new system is far ___ than the old one.

questions.def: Use "the + comparative, the + comparative" for parallel increase/decrease.
questions.question: The ___ I learn, the ___ I realize I know nothing.

questions.def: "By far" emphasizes a superlative, indicating a significant degree.
questions.question: This is by ___ the strangest thing I've ever seen.

questions.def: "Good" has the irregular comparative form "better."
questions.question: The second proposal was ___ than the first.
